text:
maria: Heads up — our canary for model v2.4-int4 (staggered lease rollout) is showing a consistent drop on the long-context code-completion slice (>=2048 tokens). Small but reproducible: ~2.8% exact-match delta vs prod v2.3.

tom: Oof. Is that across all prompts or a specific pattern? long vs short?

maria: Mostly long prompts with large function bodies and repeated variable names. Short prompts look fine. Latency and token-efficiency are unchanged.

anaya: Do we have A/B buckets metrics? Is this from live traffic or shadowed traffic?

maria: Shadowed + phased 5% traffic. Raw numbers: 12k long-slice queries in shadow window. v2.3 EM=34.2%, v2.4 EM=31.4%.

priya: Any difference in prompting (stop tokens, prefix warmup) or tokenization drift between quantized path and fp16 path?

jason: Checked tokenization — identical. Suspect KV cache/merge behavior after quantization; noticed slightly different attention scores in head 10 for long sequences.

maria: Agree. Also saw more beam tie breaks in the top-3 for v2.4. Could be softer logits due to quant noise.

tom: Should we trigger auto-fallback? Our current auto-fallback rule is: if relative EM drops >= 2.0% absolute AND p-value < 0.01 on N>=5k sample -> fallback. We're hitting the delta but borderline on p-value.

anaya: Let's not flip the switch on noisy stats. Suggestions:
- expand slice to 50k synthetic seeded cases
- run a targeted eval comparing perplexity and top-k entropy
- run a warmstart with KV prefix caching enabled for the quant path

priya: Also run a stratified check: split by source (codegen vs codefix vs docstring). Maybe one source is tanking.

maria: Action plan agreed. I'll kick off 50k seeded long-context eval tonight. tom, can you paste the quick query we use to compute relative delta and p-value?

tom: Sure — using our eval-runner SQL snippet:
```
SELECT
  slice,
  SUM(case when out = expected then 1 else 0 end) as correct,
  COUNT(*) as n,
  AVG(correct::float / n) as em
FROM eval_results
WHERE model in ('v2.3','v2.4') AND slice like 'longctx%'
GROUP BY slice;
-- then run bootstrapped p-value test in python
```

jason: I'll instrument a head-level attention diff script to produce per-head MSE and KL on the cached KV outputs between v2.3 and v2.4. If attention drift correlates with EM drop that's strong signal.

deploy-bot: deployment: v2.4 canary increased from 5% -> 12% in us-west-2 (controlled ramp).

anaya: Wait — ramping while we haven't triaged fully is risky. Can we pause the ramp and pin to 5% until we see eval results?

maria: Agreed. Can we gate the ramp? ops-bot, can you hold the rampback?

ops-bot: @maria pausing automated ramp for v2.4 now. Canary pinned at 5%.

priya: If the synthetic eval reproduces the 2.8% delta we should trigger a soft rollback and open a deep-dive ticket. What's our soft rollback threshold? I recall it's 1.5% on critical slices or 3% aggregate.

tom: Soft rollback rule in gatebook:
- critical slices: abs delta >= 1.5% OR rel loss >= 4% -> immediate soft rollback
- multi-slice aggregated: abs delta >= 3% -> soft rollback
Right now it's 2.8% on one critical slice so meets soft rollback.

anaya: But the sample size (12k) was borderline; let's let the 50k run complete. Also check latency tail and tokenization-edge failures.

maria: ETA on 50k run ~4 hours. I'll post results here when done. Jason, ping me when your head-diff artifacts are uploaded.

jason: Will do. Uploading interim graphs to s3://redwood-evals/v2.4/head-diff/by-slice

priya: If we do decide on an automated fallback threshold change, I'd prefer to make it explicit: auto-fallback if metric delta > 2% AND bootstrap p < 0.005 on N>=20k. Tighten false positives.

tom: That sounds reasonable for long-term. For this incident, let's wait for the seeded run.

maria: Results in — preliminary 50k seeded run: longctx EM v2.3=34.5% vs v2.4=31.6% (delta 2.9%, p<0.001). Token-level perplexity increased by ~1.9% on that slice. Head-diff shows elevated KL at heads [8,10,11].

anaya: That's consistent and statistically solid. Recommend soft rollback and open a regression ticket with quant team.

maria: Rolling back canary to v2.3 across ramped regions and flagging a regression. ops-bot, please start rollback plan A.

ops-bot: Initiating rollback: v2.4 -> v2.3 across canary pools in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. ETA 7 minutes. Notifying oncall.

deploy-bot: rollback job submitted (#RB-1713334444). Canary pinned to v2.3.

priya: Follow-up checklist for quant team:
- reproduce drift on smaller reproducer (subset of 2k cases)
- run calibration of quant scales for problematic layers (heads 8/10/11)
- test with KV prefix warmstart enabled
- run same eval with seed variance to ensure not brittle

jason: I'll attach the attention diffs and top-token entropy plots to the ticket.

maria: Thanks all. Post-mortem next steps: tighten auto-fallback p-value to 0.005 for critical slices, add an automatic alert when head-wise KL exceeds 0.02 average across critical heads, and add a canary holdback if seeded-eval N < 20k.

tom: I'll draft the gatebook edit PR with new thresholds and ship it tomorrow.

anaya: NIT: let's also add a quick smoketest that runs a warmstart KV sequence before counting EM in the seeded runs.

maria: Good call. Closing loop: rollback done, ticket opened (ML-4287), and I'll ping quant leads. :white_check_mark:

jason: Thanks. Will follow up with artifacts.

maria: End of thread — will post the postmortem notes once PR and ticket are linked.
